proof:
Source: Step 4 of the parent proof (the density dichotomy). It is the spherical adaptation of Dall'Alba, Lemma 4.15 and Theorem 4.16 (https://www.math.unipd.it/~monti/tesi/DallAlba.pdf; cf. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Ch. 18), stated here for an arbitrary finite measure σ, set S and outer measure m. In the parent, σ = Hⁿ⌞S(H), S = S(H) and m is the double-cone outer measure.

Notation: E := Rn N; |·| is the norm; B(x, ρ) and B̄(x, ρ) are the open and closed balls; ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal; all values of σ and m lie in [0, ∞]. For G ⊆ E let Exc(G) := {θ ∈ G : neither (α) nor (β) holds at θ}. Whether (α) or (β) holds at θ depends only on θ, m, S and n, not on F.

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Put C₂ := max(C₁, 0) ≥ 0. Since ofReal is monotone, (U) holds with C₂ in place of C₁.
 (b) Let θ ∈ S and 0 < ρ ≤ 1. Then B(θ, ρ) ⊆ B̄(θ, ρ) ⊆ B(θ, 2ρ). By (L) and by (U) at radius 2ρ, 0 < ofReal(c₁ρⁿ) ≤ σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) ≤ ofReal(C₂(2ρ)ⁿ) < ∞; here ofReal(c₁ρⁿ) > 0 because c₁ρⁿ > 0.
 (c) m is monotone, with m(∅) = 0 and m(X ∪ Y) ≤ m(X) + m(Y). For every countable index set I, m(⋃_{i∈I} X_i) ≤ Σ_{i∈I} m(X_i) (Mathlib measure_biUnion_le).
 (d) σ is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence weakly regular. So for every Borel G and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed G′ ⊆ G with σ(G ∖ G′) < ε (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt).
 (e) E is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is proper, separable, second countable and has the Besicovitch covering property. σ is finite, hence locally finite.

1. Reduction to closed F. Assume the statement holds for every closed F′ ⊆ S with m(F′) = 0; steps 2–5 prove this. Let F ⊆ S be Borel with m(F) = 0.
 By 0(d), for each k ∈ ℕ choose a closed F̃_k ⊆ F with σ(F ∖ F̃_k) < 1/(k + 1). Then F̃_k ⊆ S and m(F̃_k) ≤ m(F) = 0, so σ(Exc(F̃_k)) = 0 by the closed case.
 Put D := F ∖ ⋃_k F̃_k. Since D ⊆ F ∖ F̃_k, σ(D) < 1/(k + 1) for every k, so σ(D) = 0.
 Every θ ∈ Exc(F) lies in D or in some F̃_k. In the latter case θ ∈ Exc(F̃_k), since the conditions on θ are the same. So Exc(F) ⊆ D ∪ ⋃_k Exc(F̃_k), a countable union of σ-null sets, and σ(Exc(F)) = 0.
 From now on F ⊆ S is closed with m(F) = 0.

2. The closed sets F_j. For each integer j ≥ 1 let F_j := {θ ∈ F : m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(jtⁿ) for all t ∈ (0, 1/j)}.
 (a) F_j ⊆ F ⊆ S, and m(F_j) ≤ m(F) = 0.
 (b) F_j is closed. Let θ ∈ closure(F_j); then θ ∈ F because F is closed. Fix t ∈ (0, 1/j) and τ with 0 < τ < 1/j − t, and pick θ′ ∈ F_j with |θ′ − θ| < τ. If |x − θ| < t then |x − θ′| < t + τ, so B(θ, t) ⊆ B(θ′, t + τ). Since t + τ ∈ (0, 1/j), m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ m(S ∩ B(θ′, t + τ)) ≤ ofReal(j(t + τ)ⁿ). The map τ ↦ ofReal(j(t + τ)ⁿ) is continuous, so letting τ → 0⁺ gives m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(jtⁿ). Hence θ ∈ F_j. So F_j is closed, in particular Borel.
 (c) If θ ∈ F and (β) fails at θ, then θ ∈ F_j for some integer j ≥ 1. The failure of (β) gives K ∈ ℝ and η > 0 with m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(Ktⁿ) for all t ∈ (0, η). Choose an integer j ≥ max(1, K, 1/η). For t ∈ (0, 1/j) we have t < 1/j ≤ η, so m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(Ktⁿ) ≤ ofReal(jtⁿ), using K ≤ j and tⁿ ≥ 0.
 Hence Exc(F) ⊆ ⋃_{j ≥ 1} {θ ∈ F_j : (α) fails at θ}. Fix an integer j ≥ 1.

3. Covering estimate. Claim: for every θ ∈ F_j and 0 < t < 1/(10j), m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · σ(B̄(θ, 2t) ∖ F_j).
 Let R := (S ∩ B(θ, t)) ∖ F_j. Since S ∩ B(θ, t) ⊆ R ∪ F_j, m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ m(R) + m(F_j) = m(R). If R = ∅ then m(R) = 0 and the claim holds. Otherwise:
 (a) For ζ ∈ R put s_ζ := infDist(ζ, F_j)/2. F_j is closed and nonempty (θ ∈ F_j) and ζ ∉ F_j, so infDist(ζ, F_j) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). Also infDist(ζ, F_j) ≤ |ζ − θ| < t. Hence 0 < s_ζ < t/2.
 (b) For ζ ∈ R, B(ζ, s_ζ) ⊆ B̄(θ, 2t) ∖ F_j. If |x − ζ| < s_ζ, then |x − θ| ≤ |x − ζ| + |ζ − θ| < t/2 + t < 2t. Also infDist(x, F_j) ≥ infDist(ζ, F_j) − |x − ζ| > 2s_ζ − s_ζ > 0, so x ∉ F_j.
 (c) Apply Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement to the balls B(ζ, s_ζ), ζ ∈ R, with δ(ζ) := s_ζ ∈ [0, t/2] and τ := 2 > 1; the balls are nonempty since ζ ∈ B(ζ, s_ζ). This gives R′ ⊆ R such that the balls B(ζ, s_ζ), ζ ∈ R′, are pairwise disjoint, and every ζ ∈ R has some ζ′ ∈ R′ with B(ζ, s_ζ) ∩ B(ζ′, s_ζ′) ≠ ∅ and s_ζ ≤ 2s_ζ′. For x in that intersection, |ζ − ζ′| ≤ |ζ − x| + |x − ζ′| < s_ζ + s_ζ′ ≤ 3s_ζ′ < 5s_ζ′. (Equivalently, Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_ball with τ = 5 gives B(ζ, s_ζ) ⊆ B(ζ′, 5s_ζ′) directly.) Since R ⊆ S, R ⊆ ⋃_{ζ′ ∈ R′} (S ∩ B(ζ′, 5s_ζ′)).
 (d) R′ is countable, because the balls B(ζ, s_ζ), ζ ∈ R′, are pairwise disjoint nonempty open sets in the separable space E (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen).
 (e) Let ζ ∈ R′. Since infDist(ζ, F_j) = 2s_ζ < 5s_ζ and F_j ≠ ∅, there is φ ∈ F_j with |ζ − φ| < 5s_ζ (Metric.infDist_lt_iff). Then B(ζ, 5s_ζ) ⊆ B(φ, 10s_ζ), and 0 < 10s_ζ < 5t < 1/(2j) < 1/j. Since φ ∈ F_j,
  m(S ∩ B(ζ, 5s_ζ)) ≤ m(S ∩ B(φ, 10s_ζ)) ≤ ofReal(j(10s_ζ)ⁿ) = ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · ofReal(c₁s_ζⁿ) ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · σ(B(ζ, s_ζ)).
  The last step uses (L) at ζ ∈ R ⊆ S with 0 < s_ζ < t/2 < 2.
 (f) Combine:
  m(R) ≤ Σ_{ζ ∈ R′} m(S ∩ B(ζ, 5s_ζ))   [(c), (d) and countable subadditivity, 0(c)]
   ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · Σ_{ζ ∈ R′} σ(B(ζ, s_ζ))   [(e) and ENNReal.tsum_mul_left]
   = ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · σ(⋃_{ζ ∈ R′} B(ζ, s_ζ))   [countable additivity on pairwise disjoint open, hence Borel, balls; measure_biUnion]
   ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · σ(B̄(θ, 2t) ∖ F_j)   [(b)].
  This proves the claim.

4. Density points. Apply the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) to the locally finite measure σ and the set F_j, using 0(e). It gives, for σ⌞F_j-a.e. θ, q_θ(ρ) := σ(F_j ∩ B̄(θ, ρ))/σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺. Since F_j is Borel, ae_restrict_iff' shows that Bad_j := {θ ∈ F_j : q_θ(ρ) does not tend to 1 as ρ → 0⁺} is σ-null. We show that (α) holds at every θ ∈ F_j ∖ Bad_j; then {θ ∈ F_j : (α) fails} ⊆ Bad_j is σ-null. Fix θ ∈ F_j ∖ Bad_j; note θ ∈ S.
 (a) Let 0 < ρ ≤ 1. By 0(b), 0 < σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) ≤ ofReal(C₂(2ρ)ⁿ) < ∞. The sets F_j ∩ B̄(θ, ρ) ⊆ B̄(θ, ρ) are Borel of finite measure, so σ(B̄(θ, ρ) ∖ F_j) = σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) − σ(F_j ∩ B̄(θ, ρ)). Since σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) · q_θ(ρ) = σ(F_j ∩ B̄(θ, ρ)), this equals σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) · (1 − q_θ(ρ)) ≤ ofReal(C₂(2ρ)ⁿ) · (1 − q_θ(ρ)).
 (b) Put M := j10ⁿ4ⁿC₂/c₁ ≥ 0. Let 0 < t < min(1/(10j), 1/2). By step 3 and (a) with ρ := 2t ∈ (0, 1],
  m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · ofReal(C₂(4t)ⁿ) · (1 − q_θ(2t)) = ofReal(tⁿ) · ofReal(M) · (1 − q_θ(2t)).
 (c) Let c > 0. As t → 0⁺ we have 2t → 0⁺, so q_θ(2t) → 1 and 1 − q_θ(2t) → 0 in [0, ∞]. Because ofReal(M) < ∞, also ofReal(M) · (1 − q_θ(2t)) → 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). Since ofReal(c) > 0, there is η with 0 < η ≤ min(1/(10j), 1/2) such that ofReal(M) · (1 − q_θ(2t)) ≤ ofReal(c) for all t ∈ (0, η). For such t, m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(tⁿ) · ofReal(c) = ofReal(ctⁿ). Thus (α) holds at θ.

5. Conclusion. For closed F, step 2(c) and step 4 give Exc(F) ⊆ ⋃_{j ≥ 1} {θ ∈ F_j : (α) fails} ⊆ ⋃_{j ≥ 1} Bad_j. This is a countable union of σ-null sets, so σ(Exc(F)) = 0. By step 1 the same holds for every Borel F ⊆ S with m(F) = 0, which is the statement σ({θ | θ ∈ F ∧ ¬(α at θ) ∧ ¬(β at θ)}) = 0. ∎
key_steps: Preliminaries: C₂ := max(C₁, 0). For θ ∈ S and 0 < ρ ≤ 1, 0 < σ(B̄(θ, ρ)) ≤ ofReal(C₂(2ρ)ⁿ) < ∞. m is monotone and countably subadditive over countable index sets, and σ is weakly regular.
Reduction to closed F: closed F̃_k ⊆ F with σ(F ∖ F̃_k) < 1/(k+1) give Exc(F) ⊆ (F ∖ ⋃_k F̃_k) ∪ ⋃_k Exc(F̃_k).
For closed F, the sets F_j := {θ ∈ F : m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(jtⁿ) for 0 < t < 1/j} are closed and m-null, and every θ ∈ F where (β) fails lies in some F_j.
Covering estimate via Vitali with radii s_ζ = infDist(ζ, F_j)/2 and the lower bound (L): m(S ∩ B(θ, t)) ≤ ofReal(j10ⁿ/c₁) · σ(B̄(θ, 2t) ∖ F_j) for θ ∈ F_j and 0 < t < 1/(10j).
Besicovitch density theorem for σ and F_j: at σ-a.e. θ ∈ F_j, σ(B̄(θ, 2t) ∖ F_j) ≤ ofReal(C₂(4t)ⁿ)(1 − q_θ(2t)) = o(tⁿ), so (α) holds there.
Exc(F) ⊆ ⋃_j Bad_j is a countable union of σ-null sets.
